text:
samantha: Quick question — I have to split my time between Portland and Seattle for March (roughly Mon/Tue in Seattle, Wed-Fri in Portland). Do I need to do anything for the WFH stipend, payroll homebase, and benefits while this split is temporary?

alex (people-ops): Thanks for flagging! Short answer: update your homebase effective date, we'll prorate the monthly WFH stipend if the change is mid-month, and payroll will adjust state tax withholding for the pay period that includes the change. Also check benefits implications below.

samantha: Got it. Is the stipend prorated automatically or do I need to file anything? My stipend is the standard internet/equipment $100/mo.

paul-payroll-bot: FYI — if a homebase change happens mid-pay-period we prorate the WFH stipend based on calendar days in each homebase. Payroll will also calculate state withholding by residence day split for that pay period. Upload the homebase change request by end of day before the pay cutoff to avoid delays.

alex (people-ops): Action items for you: 1) Submit the "Homebase Change" form (HR > Relocations) with effective date 2026-03-01. 2) Add notes about the weekly split so we have documentation. 3) If you expect >30 days total in the non-primary state this quarter, flag it — that can create tax nexus and we may need to register payroll in that state.

jordan (benefits): Also adding: short, temporary splits usually don't break benefits eligibility, but if you move your legal residence or enroll an address change in the benefits portal it can trigger carrier rules. For health insurance, coverage follows your enrolled address; a temporary split is fine but please don't update residency unless permanent.

samantha: Okay — the split is temporary (just March). I won't change legal residence. What's the deadline for the payroll cutoff?

paul-payroll-bot: Payroll cutoff for the March 15 pay period is 2026-03-05 11:59pm PT. If we receive the form after cutoff, the change will process on the next pay period and stipend/taxes will be applied then.

alex (people-ops): If the split is only one month we'll do the proration and no further actions. If plans change and you stay >90 days in the other state, ping us and we'll walk through state registration and permanent payroll updates.

emily: Quick note on travel vs homebase — if you only travel for work (company trip) and temporary hotel stays, that doesn't count as homebase. The determinant is where you sleep regularly and your declared homebase in HR.

samantha: Thanks — submitting form now. One last thing: will I still get the full internet stipend for March if I move mid-month but expenses stay the same?

alex (people-ops): Per policy we prorate by days in each homebase. If you prefer to keep it simple, we can manually keep full stipend for this one-off month — just say so in your form and we'll make a note. For audit reasons we prefer documenting exceptions.

samantha: I'll request full stipend in the form and add note that expenses unchanged. Thanks everyone! :pray:

alex (people-ops): Got it — we'll process and confirm once payroll finalizes. Expect an email thread with the updated paystub and stipend breakdown after payroll runs.

paul-payroll-bot: Reminder posted to payroll queue: process homebase change for samantha, effective 2026-03-01.

jordan (benefits): If anything changes on the benefits side I'll DM you directly.

samantha: Appreciate it — closing the loop here.
